hypotheses.title: Better Choices → Better Lives → Better Markets → A Better World
hypotheses.statement: Better information and better alternatives can improve individual outcomes; at sufficient scale, changed choices redirect demand and capital, changing market incentives and potentially producing better planetary outcomes.
falsifiers: better information does not materially change decisions
changed demand does not alter relevant firm incentives
market changes do not improve the measured planetary outcome
hypotheses.originality_note: Long-running founder theory and central 4PLANET synthesis; causal links must be evidenced separately.

hypotheses.title: Money Is a Language
hypotheses.statement: Spending, procurement and investment are allocation signals that markets can respond to through revenue, margins, valuation and cost of capital.
falsifiers: allocation shifts are too small or constrained to affect incentives

hypotheses.title: Self-Interest Can Be Planetary Infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Environmental action can scale when a better planetary choice is also better for the decision-maker: healthier, cheaper, easier, safer, more resilient or more profitable.
falsifiers: aligned personal benefits do not improve adoption or persistence

hypotheses.title: The Transparency Dividend
hypotheses.statement: In evidence-based decision systems, verifiable transparency can become economically advantageous because it enables higher-confidence evaluation; opacity remains UNKNOWN rather than being treated as proven harm.
falsifiers: decision systems do not reward verifiable evidence
transparency has no material effect on buyer, procurement or capital decisions

hypotheses.title: Truth by Design: I Don’t Know Is a Feature
hypotheses.statement: Trustworthy intelligence should structurally preserve UNKNOWN, conflicts, limitations and uncertainty rather than fill gaps with confidence theatre.
falsifiers: explicit uncertainty consistently reduces decision quality more than false precision alternatives

hypotheses.title: Don’t Score the World
hypotheses.statement: A universal moral or ESG number often hides incompatible values, scope and uncertainty; decision quality can improve when material dimensions and trade-offs remain visible.
falsifiers: well-defined single scores outperform multidimensional explanations across the intended decision domains without material information loss

hypotheses.title: Personal Decision Infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: A useful environmental interface may be a personal decision assistant that treats planetary consequences as one normal dimension of everyday decision quality rather than as a separate climate application.
falsifiers: users do not value or use planetary information when integrated into everyday decisions

hypotheses.title: Better Information Changes Selection Pressure
hypotheses.statement: Information, standards and transparency can change which company and product traits receive demand and capital, changing what firms compete to optimise.
falsifiers: information improvements do not alter competitive selection in measured cases
hypotheses.originality_note: Biological selection is an analogy, not evidence of economic causality.

hypotheses.title: Nature Is Part of the Economic System
hypotheses.statement: Companies, products and economies depend on living systems, places, water, climate regulation, species functions and material flows; nature intelligence therefore belongs inside economic decisions rather than only in CSR reporting.
falsifiers: material economic dependencies on natural systems are absent in the relevant decision domain

hypotheses.title: From Reporting to Proof
hypotheses.statement: Sustainability reporting becomes more decision-useful when material claims are traceable to documents, systems, external evidence, assurance and where appropriate physical or remote verification.
falsifiers: traceable claim-level provenance does not improve assurance or decision usefulness

hypotheses.title: The Honest Company Advantage
hypotheses.statement: As buyers, AI systems, procurement and capital demand evidence, companies able to prove what they do may gain trust, distribution or capital advantages.
falsifiers: verified honesty/transparency provides no measurable advantage in relevant markets

hypotheses.title: Culture → Attention → Capital → Action → Impact
hypotheses.statement: Culture can shape attention; attention can mobilise people and capital; resources enable action; action only becomes impact when outcomes are demonstrated.
falsifiers: the proposed links do not hold in measured activation cases

hypotheses.title: If You Live on This Planet, You Can Help It
hypotheses.statement: Planetary action can be designed so people and institutions participate according to their capabilities rather than requiring activist or specialist identity.
falsifiers: lower-friction inclusive participation does not increase useful action

hypotheses.title: Separate Worlds. Shared Infrastructure. Controlled Depth.
hypotheses.statement: Distinct audiences need clear interfaces while identity, evidence and engines should be shared where appropriate; complexity belongs underneath and depth should match user need.
falsifiers: shared infrastructure creates greater user/system harm than separated stacks in the intended architecture

hypotheses.title: The Reality Layer
hypotheses.statement: AI is more trustworthy when it interprets a governed reality layer containing sources, provenance, conflicts, methods, uncertainty, decisions and learning rather than acting as the source of truth itself.
falsifiers: a governed provenance layer does not materially improve factual reliability, recoverability or auditability
